GenAI Basics • Lesson 10 • Module 3: own models

Open models

How to run a language model on your laptop and on a rented GPU

Hugging Face, LM Studio, Ollama, RunPod. Model size, memory, speed, price. Data as of October 2026.

← → navigate • N speaker notes • G all slides • F fullscreen
The idea

One app, three places where the model runs

1Cloud API: the vendor runs the model; you pay per token and your data goes to them
2Your laptop (localhost = “this computer”): the model file is yours, no internet needed, you pay with hardware
3Rented GPU: your model on someone else’s powerful machine, paid by the hour
Key point: the app’s code barely changes; only the address it sends the request to does.

Open model

An open model is a file you can download, plus its licence

Hugging Face · ibm-granite/granite-4.2-8b-GGUF · captured 16.10.2026
1
2
3
1Who made it: IBM, Granite 4.2 8B. 8B = 8 billion parameters, the numbers inside the model
2Licence Apache-2.0: fine for work and commercial use
3.gguf files (the format for LM Studio and Ollama): one model in several sizes, here 5.35 to 9.35 GB
Hugging Face is the main “warehouse” of open models. Each has a card: what it does, its limits, its licence.
“Open” ≠ “anything goes”. Llama 4 has its own restrictive licence; MusicGen (L06) is non-commercial only.

Why

Your own model: data stays home, but quality trails the leaders

Pros: data never leaves the machine · works offline · no per-token bill · nobody changes the model behind your back
Cons: weaker than the best cloud models · needs memory and a GPU · setup and updates are your job
Good for: sorting emails and tickets, drafts, search over your own documents. Poor at: hard reasoning, large codebases.

How it fits together

Five parts: file, engine, hardware, server, app

The engine (llama.cpp) reads the model file and computes the answer. The server gives it an address, just like a cloud API.
If it is slow, find which part is to blame: file too big? no GPU? Not “the model is bad”.

The model file plus room for the conversation must fit the GPU memory

on top of the file: memory for the context, the conversation history (usually 20–30%)
GPU memory (VRAM): 6 GB → up to 4B · 16 GB → up to 12B · 24 GB → up to 27B.
Without a GPU the model lives in system RAM: it fits, but runs slowly. Take 3–4B.

Local server

Turn on the server and the model answers your code like a cloud API

Python, the same code as in L03
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="http://localhost:1234/v1",
    api_key="lm-studio")                # for the cloud: your key

r = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="granite-4.2-3b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": ticket}])
print(r.choices[0].message.content)
Only the address and model name change (and the key)
Cloud (OpenAI)
https://api.openai.com/v1
gpt-5.4-mini
Laptop (LM Studio)
http://localhost:1234/v1
granite-4.2-3b
Laptop (Ollama)
http://localhost:11434/v1
granite4.2:3b
In LM Studio: Developer → Start server. The address localhost means “this computer”.

Hands-on with an agent

A coding agent installs the model for you and measures the speed

Prompt for Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity
Install Ollama on this computer (official installer from ollama.com) and run the open model granite4.2:3b.
1. Check the GPU and its memory, system RAM and free disk. Tell me which model fits.
2. Download the model and ask it: “Briefly: what is quantisation?”
3. Measure the speed (tokens per second) and how much memory the model uses.
4. Show the local server address and give me an example request in Python.
5. Expose nothing to the network; the server stays on localhost only.
Ollama — a similar tool that is easy to drive with commands: ollama run granite4.2:3b.
The agent checks the hardware, installs the program, downloads the model and reports back: speed, memory, server address.
The agent installs software on your computer: read what it proposes to run and approve each step.

Security

“Local” does not automatically mean “private”: check the whole data path

The model computes on your machine
the request text goes nowhere
Model downloads and updates
go to the internet; download from official sources
Plug-ins and web search
may send data outside
Server exposed to the network (not localhost)
others can reach the model; turn on Require Authentication
Class rule: server on localhost only, models only from Hugging Face by known publishers, client documents only with permission.
The model licence is part of security too: do not “accidentally” ship a non-commercial model in a product.

Laptop limits

When a laptop is not enough: four signs

Does not fit
the model is bigger than the laptop’s memory
Too slow
10,000 emails overnight is too much for a CPU
Many users
one laptop serves one person
Needs 24/7
laptops get closed and taken home
Solution: keep the same model and the same code, but move the computing to a powerful cloud GPU. Only the address changes.

RunPod

RunPod: a GPU rented with per-second billing, two modes

runpod.io/pricing · Community Cloud · captured 16.10.2026
Green: RTX 4090, 24 GB — $0.34 per hour
One working day of a support bot
Pod
on in the morning, off in the evening: you pay all 9 hours, lunch included
Serverless
the GPU wakes per request: you pay only those minutes
00:0006:0012:0018:00
Trap: a stopped Pod (Stop) still bills for its disk. When you are done, delete it (Terminate).

How to choose

Choose by two questions: can the data leave, and how much work is there

Few requests
Many requests
Data may go to the model vendor
Cloud API
ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude: best quality, pay per request
Cloud API
the vendor’s batch processing is usually cheaper than renting
Data must stay with you
Your laptop
LM Studio, Ollama
RunPod
Pod for a steady flow; Serverless for bursts
RunPod is also someone else’s computer, but the model and data are under your control, not the model vendor’s. Keep the code so the address changes with one line.

Homework

Homework: run a model yourself and compare it honestly with the cloud

  1. Install LM Studio or Ollama; download a 3–9B model at Q4
  2. Give it 3 work tasks, and the same tasks to ChatGPT or Gemini
  3. Record the speed (tokens/s) and the memory the model uses
  4. Score the answers 1–5 and draw a conclusion
  5. Fill the card: API / laptop / Pod / Serverless and why
L10_homework/
├─ README.md          # choice and conclusion
├─ results.md         # 3 tasks: local vs cloud
├─ speed.png          # screenshot with tokens/s
└─ decision.md        # decision card
No suitable computer? Take the smallest model (Granite 4.2 3B, 2.2 GB); it runs without a GPU.
Synthetic or your own data only. RunPod is optional and paid.
